who: Historian of colonial Virginia, University of Georgia professor, 1964–1988; PhD University of Virginia.

evidence.says: The authority for G. Melvin Herndon cites Financing the Revolution in Va. (1981), identifying its author as professor of history at the University of Georgia; variants include George Melvin Herndon.
The Athens Banner-Herald obituary identifies G. Melvin Herndon as a University of Virginia PhD and University of Georgia history professor from 1964 to 1988.

notes: The LC record explicitly supplies the students' institution during the supervision period; the obituary independently matches the doctorate institution.

who: Historian at North Texas State University / University of North Texas; PhD Duke University, 1963.

evidence.says: The Bullitt Lowry authority cites his contribution to The memoirs of Louise Michel, the Red Virgin (1981).
The publisher identifies editor and translator Bullitt Lowry as associate professor of history at North Texas State University.
The generals, the Armistice, and the Treaty of Versailles, 1919, by Francis Bullitt Lowry, was originally a Duke University PhD thesis, 1963.
UNT's history department records document Francis Bullitt Lowry's promotion and tenure, including materials from 1988–1994; the finding aid explains the university's 1988 name change.

notes: The authority's work connects directly to the North Texas historian; the full-name dissertation record matches the AHA doctorate.

who: Noel J. Stowe, public historian at Arizona State University; PhD history, University of Southern California, 1970.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Noel J. Stowe as author of California government (1975).

ASU's December 2008 memorial states that Stowe joined its history faculty in 1967, chaired the department in 1998–2007, directed graduate dissertations, and earned his USC history doctorate in 1970. It names the Noel J. Stowe public history endowment.

notes: Full name, institution, supervision period and exact doctorate institution/year agree.

who: E. Jane Errington, historian of colonial North America at Queen's University; PhD Queen's University.

evidence.says: Queen's identifies Jane Errington as a professor with a Queen's PhD, researching colonial North America and British North America and supervising graduate work in those fields.
The 2016 supervision award profile states that Jane Errington had joined Queen's more than twenty years earlier and had supervised seventeen PhD students to completion.
The candidate authority is Elizabeth Errington, also E. A. (Elizabeth A.) Errington, associated with The Crossroads of Asia (1992) and Gandharan Buddhist reliquaries (2012).
The Smithsonian catalogue for Gandharan Buddhist reliquaries identifies Elizabeth Errington as curator of the Charles Masson Project in the British Museum Department of Coins and Medals.

notes: The sole candidate is the Gandhara archaeologist and numismatist Elizabeth A. Errington, a different scholar from Queen's colonial historian E. Jane Errington.

who: David Sherman Lovejoy, early American historian at Wisconsin–Madison, 1960–1983; PhD Brown University, 1954.

evidence.says: Wisconsin's memorial identifies David S. Lovejoy as David Sherman Lovejoy, records his Brown history PhD in 1954 and Wisconsin faculty service from 1960 until retirement in 1983, and names Religious Enthusiasm in the New World among his books.
The authority equates David S. Lovejoy with David Sherman Lovejoy and cites Religious enthusiasm in the new world (1985).

notes: Full name, distinctive work, exact doctorate and Wisconsin service spanning the listed dissertations establish the candidate match.

who: Marlene Gay Shore, intellectual and cultural historian at York University; PhD University of Toronto.

evidence.says: The Marlene Gay Shore authority cites The science of social redemption (1987), whose title page uses Marlene Shore.
York's 1999 Gazette identifies Marlene Shore as a history professor and acting graduate history director, and as author of The Science of Social Redemption.
Toronto's Senior College profile states that Shore received her BA and PhD at Toronto and continues supervising York doctoral candidates after retiring as professor of history.
Alexander Hughes's dissertation acknowledgements identify Marlene Shore as his supervisor and describe her supervision beginning during his preparations for doctoral work at York.

notes: The LC name variant is bridged by the same book; university sources confirm the affiliation, doctorate institution and direct supervision of a listed student.

who: Robert A. Trennert, historian of the American West and American Indian history at Arizona State University; PhD UCSB, 1969.

evidence.says: The Robert A. Trennert authority cites Alternative to extinction (1975) and White man's medicine (1998); the latter supplies the fuller name Robert Anthony Trennert.

The Western History Association identifies Trennert as an ASU historian who completed his UCSB graduate degree in 1969, retired from ASU teaching in 2003, and served on graduate committees. It lists Alternative to Extinction and White Man's Medicine among his books.

notes: The authority's two books identify the same ASU historian; the doctorate and teaching period agree with the AHA records.

who: Sally N. Vaughn, medieval historian at the University of Houston; PhD UCSB, 1978.

evidence.says: The Sally N. Vaughn authority cites The Abbey of Bec and the Anglo-Norman state and Anselm of Bec and Robert of Meulan; the latter uses Sally Vaughn.
Houston identifies Sally Vaughn as its medieval history professor emeritus, with a UCSB PhD, and lists both books cited in the authority.
UCSB's October 1988 history newsletter identifies Sally Vaughn as PhD '78 and associate professor of history at Houston.
Houston's PhD graduates list names Sally Vaughn as advisor for Julie Sarpy, Holle Canatella, Courtney DeMayo and Benjamin Pugno, with dissertation titles matching the supplied records.

notes: Name variants and books connect the LC candidate to Houston; exact doctorate year and several listed advisees independently confirm the match.
